era: E0 1842-1959 foundations: guided light, field theory, waveguides, maser
event: Proposes transporting optical images through bundles of thin transparent fibres; fibres coated with a lower-index layer (total reflexion) gave flexible 'image rods' with satisfactory transmission.
notes: Nature No. 4392, 2 January 1954, p.39 (page header); the letter's dateline prints 'May 21.' with no year, and no received date. Scan with OCR (1 page): the OCR interleaves this letter with W. L. Roth's preceding letter and the following Hopkins-Kapany fibrescope letter; values read from page_01.png: core index 1.52, coating 1.47, effective angular aperture about 1:1.8, core down to 0.1 mm, low-index coating at least three to five wavelengths thick, samples 6 to 20 cm long, bendable up to at least 360 deg; preliminary experiments started January 1950; silver/metal coating unsatisfactory; plastic fibres transmitted better than the first glass models. The letter has no figure: Fig. 4 on the same page belongs to Roth's letter, so the key-figure fields are empty. The paper makes no 'first' claim. Work done under contract with the National Defence Research Council; no acknowledgment of persons. No component rows: fibre bundle (fibers are not a component class) and no quantitative transmission or loss value.

era: E1 1960-1969 laser, nonlinear optics, integrated-optics idea
event: Reports observation of the second harmonic near 3472 A produced by projecting an intense 6943 A ruby optical-maser beam through crystalline quartz.
orgs_printed: The Harrison M. Randall Laboratory of Physics, The University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, Michigan
key_figure_caption: Spectrographic plate, scale in 100 A units: an arrow marks the small dense second-harmonic image at 3472 A; the 6943 A primary-beam image is enlarged by halation.
key_figure_reason: the plate the letter presents as evidence of the second harmonic
notes: Received 1961-07-21 (p.1). PRL vol. 7 no. 4, 15 August 1961, pp.118-119 = text.md pp.1-2. text.md p.3 has no text: the PDF's third page holds a higher-resolution copy of Fig. 1 (img_p03_1.png, used as key_figure_file; the printed figure is on p.2, also in page_02.png). Byline P. A. Franken, A. E. Hill, C. W. Peters, G. Weinreich; the paper states no individual roles, so the papers.csv DRI (Franken) is kept but is not confirmed by the paper. The caption's 'first plate' refers to the authors' first exposure, not a priority claim. Values read from the renders: about 3 J in a 1 ms pulse from a commercial ruby optical maser (Trion Instruments Model TO-3000), order of 10^11 second-harmonic photons per pulse estimated from plate density (p.2). Supported in part by the U.S. Atomic Energy Commission; thanks the staff of Trion Instruments (p.2). No component rows: the converter is a bulk crystalline quartz sample (D411, out of scope) and no conversion efficiency is stated.

era: E1 1960-1969 laser, nonlinear optics, integrated-optics idea
event: Reports continuous-wave optical maser oscillation at five near-infrared wavelengths in a He-Ne discharge, strongest 15 mW at 11530 A; claims first gaseous optical-frequency maser.
dri: A. Javan; W. R. Bennett; D. R. Herriott
dri_locator: p.1 byline (A. Javan, W. R. Bennett, Jr., D. R. Herriott); p.5 excitation-transfer principle suggested by one of the authors (refs. 1-2, Javan)
orgs_printed: Bell Telephone Laboratories, Murray Hill, New Jersey
key_figure_caption: Near-field (pattern in maser cavity, 0.45 inch marker) and far-field (angular distribution, 1 minute of arc marker) photographs of the beam with plates parallel and at 6 seconds angle.
key_figure_reason: the CW output beam: narrow pattern, under one minute of arc spread
notes: Received 1960-12-30 (p.1). PRL vol. 6 no. 3, 1 February 1961, pp.106-110 = text.md pp.1-5; p.1 opens with the end of a preceding letter and p.5 ends with the start of the Barnes-Martin-McDaniel letter. text.md pp.6-8 have no text: the PDF's last three pages hold higher-resolution copies of Figs. 2, 3, 4 (img_p06_1, img_p07_1, img_p08_1); key_figure_file img_p06_1.png is Fig. 2, printed on p.3 (also in page_03.png). 'First' claim: 'the first gaseous system which has led to maser oscillations at optical frequencies' (p.5). Values from renders: 0.1 mm Hg Ne + 1 mm Hg He, quartz tube 1.5 cm ID x 80 cm, plate separation 1 m, 28 Mc/s excitation, about 50 W dissipation; plates with 13-layer evaporated dielectric films, reflectance 98.9 % with 0.3 % transmission over 11000-12000 A (p.3); lines 11180, 11530, 11600, 11990, 12070 A; linewidth 10-80 kc/s from beat notes (p.1, p.5, Fig. 4). Acknowledgments: co-workers F. Muller, P. S. Kubik, A. R. Strnad, D. MacNair, E. Koch, G. J. Wolff, G. E. Reitter; A. F. Turner of Bausch & Lomb supplied the reflectance films; E. A. Ballik assisted in the later stages (p.5). DRI unchanged. No component rows: bulk gas laser (out of the component taxonomy) and its Fabry-Perot plates are bulk mirrors with supplied coatings (D411).
